cop.why: The law faction and its archetype already read 'Spore Warden' in both swamp packs.

police.why: Mass noun for the same faction; the colony has wardens, not police.

thug.why: The melee archetype is drawn and named 'Bog Mutant' (bog-mutant cast walk).

gangster.why: The pistol hunter is the Rootcult's; acolyte names a cult member without modern crime.

enforcer.why: 'Rootcult Enforcer' is mob-muscle wording for the same archetype.

gang.why: The hostile-on-sight faction is mostly swamp life (Mireclaw, Cinder Husks, sporelings), not a street gang.

bouncer.why: The peaceful-until-hit door guard is drawn as the 'Airlock Warden'; a lockkeeper keeps the airlock.

officer.why: The raid's command role is the Tide Bellwether, the bell that leads the flock.

heist.why: The bunker objective run is a colony salvage dive, not a robbery.

crime.why: Attacking settlers in view of the wardens; a misdeed carries no police-procedural frame.

criminal.why: Who the wardens chase; no legal-system frame.

law.why: 'The law' means the warden faction; the colony keeps a watch (the art lore's Sodium Watch).

lawful.why: Hostility value for wardens: only aggro on troublemakers.

robber.why: Cops-and-robbers framing; raiders are the tide's word.

thief.why: Settlers in the lore scavenge; a thief is street-crime.

dcop.why: Test-local delta variable fused with cop.

dthug.why: Test-local delta variable fused with thug.

dgang.why: Test-local delta variable fused with gang.

street.why: The outdoor floors are a sunken colony; its open ground is raised causeways over bog, not Earth streets.

sidewalk.why: The walkway beside a causeway is a boardwalk over the swamp.

briefcase.why: The objective already reads 'Specimen Canister' to players; 'keycard' is taken by the wing keycard archetype.

bat.why: Colony melee is its maintenance kit; the lore-weapons work makes the bat a pipe wrench (wrench essence = weight/knockback).

scoped.why: The old base theme pack: the drowned settlement as built, before the swamp (LORE: a colony 'physically sinking into the swamp'). Scoped because 'city' elsewhere names the sunken-city floors, which stay.

phrases.from:
* Lore names for the four sim FACTION ids. The ids themselves are load-bearing
 * (`entity.Faction`, the disposition matrix, the BLE snapshot), so they stay —
 * this is the player-facing half only. Without it the inspect card printed a
 * bare `Faction: Gang` on a derelict swamp station, which is exactly the
 * cops-and-robbers vocabulary the theme has otherwise moved past. Wording is
 * taken from the shipped manifest so the card agrees with the name plates:
 * `Rootcult Enforcer`, `Spore Warden`, `Settler`.
phrases.to:
* Lore names for the four sim FACTION ids (`entity.Faction`, the disposition
 * matrix, the BLE snapshot). The ids are terse; this is the player-facing half.
 * Wording is taken from the shipped manifest so the card agrees with the name
 * plates: `Rootcult Acolyte`, `Spore Warden`, `Settler`.
phrases.why: inspectModel.ts: the old comment explained the label by quoting the old id, which the rename makes untrue.

phrases.to: // The card prints the faction's lore name, never the terse sim id.
